qs.e: Abdominal bracing during shifting and hesitation before standing are the assigned cues. The other behaviors portray different communication scenarios.

qs.q: “It’s not that bad, is it?” is an example of a ______ question.
qs.e: A leading question suggests the answer the nurse expects. A neutral question instead asks about the client's pain without supplying the answer.

qs.q: A teen reports hurtful body comments at school, disliking the mirror, and skipping lunch. Which response is most appropriate?
c: “Those comments sound hurtful and embarrassing.”
“You look fine, so there is no reason to worry.”
“Let me quickly ask every personal question before we talk.”
“Your appearance is the real issue.”
qs.e: An empathetic statement acknowledges hurt and embarrassment without judging appearance. Appearance-based reassurance is specifically discouraged.

qs.q: Which approaches are appropriate for the teen with eating changes and intense body dissatisfaction? Select all that apply.
c: Provide sensitive follow-up.
Arrange appropriate assessment.
Acknowledge hurt without judging appearance.
Offer appearance-based reassurance.
Reinforce weight stigma.
qs.e: Eating changes and intense body dissatisfaction warrant sensitive follow-up and assessment. Reassurance based on appearance and weight stigma are not appropriate substitutes.

qs.q: Which nursing behavior demonstrates intrusive or premature probing?
c: Acknowledging the teen's embarrassment
Establishing trust before exploring personal concerns
Rapidly asking prying personal questions before establishing trust
Responding sensitively to reported eating changes
qs.e: Rapid personal questioning that feels prying before trust is established is the specified nontherapeutic behavior. Appropriate assessment is still needed, but it should be sensitive.

qs.q: Which acting cues are specified for the teen with body image concerns?
c: Avoid eye contact and pull sleeves over the hands.
Fold the arms and express frustration about pills.
Reach toward the nurse, then hesitate.
Look around and attempt to stand in fear.
qs.e: Avoiding eye contact and pulling sleeves over the hands are this teen's cues. Reaching toward the nurse belongs to the client afraid of dying.

qs.q: The designated therapeutic response that acknowledges the teen's hurt and embarrassment is an ______.
qs.e: An empathetic statement acknowledges the emotional experience without judging appearance. Saying the teen looks fine is appearance-based reassurance rather than the requested response.

qs.q: A client with advanced illness says, “I’m scared of dying,” and reaches toward the nurse, then hesitates. What is the most appropriate action?
c: Take the client's hand without asking.
Ask permission before offering a hand and respect the response.
Tell a lengthy story about the nurse's own experience.
Assume touch will comfort every client.
qs.e: Therapeutic touch requires permission and respect for the client's response. Reaching and then hesitating does not replace asking.

qs.q: Which considerations should guide the nurse's use of touch with the client afraid of dying? Select all that apply.
c: Consent
Culture
Trauma history
The client's cues
The assumption that touch is universally comforting
qs.e: The slide identifies consent, culture, trauma history, and client cues as considerations. Touch is not universally comforting.

qs.q: A nurse responds to a client's fear of dying by telling a personal story that shifts attention to the nurse. How should this response be evaluated?
c: It is the designated therapeutic technique.
It is nontherapeutic talking about yourself.
It demonstrates permission for touch.
It presents reality and reorientation.
qs.e: The problem is shifting attention away from the client through the nurse's own story. The scenario calls for remaining present with the client's experience.

qs.q: A client does not want touch while discussing fear of dying. Which actions remain appropriate? Select all that apply.
c: Respect the client's response.
Remain present.
Listen.
Insist that touch will help.
Withdraw support because touch was declined.
qs.e: Presence and listening are alternatives to touch, and the client's response must be respected. Declining touch is not a reason to withdraw support.

qs.q: In the afraid-of-dying role-play, the client speaks ______ and reaches toward the nurse before hesitating.
qs.e: Quiet speech, reaching toward the nurse, and hesitation are the assigned cues. These cues do not remove the need to obtain permission before touch.

qs.q: A postoperative client reports pain of zero while grimacing and guarding the incision. Which response best demonstrates making observations?
c: “You are not being honest about your pain.”
“I noticed you grimaced and guarded your incision when moving. Can you tell me about that?”
“Your pain must be severe because of your appearance.”
“You said zero, so no further assessment is needed.”
qs.e: Making observations describes specific behaviors without accusation and invites explanation. Neither dismissing the behaviors nor assigning pain solely from appearance follows the slide.

qs.q: Which behaviors accompany the client's report of zero pain in this scenario? Select all that apply.
c: Grimacing
Guarding the incision
Grunting when moving
Holding a tissue while grieving
Looking at a phone and shrugging
qs.e: Grimacing, guarding the incision, and grunting with movement are the specified behaviors. They invite further assessment rather than automatic rejection of the client's self-report.

qs.q: Which nursing action requires follow-up when the client reports zero pain but shows discomfort while changing position?
c: Respecting the self-report while assessing further
Inviting the client to explain the observed behavior
Accepting the number without further assessment
Using an open, culturally responsive approach
qs.e: Accepting the number without further assessment ignores the nonverbal cues. Respecting self-report is compatible with exploring the discrepancy.

qs.q: Which statement indicates understanding of the clinical note about mismatched pain reports and behavior?
c: “Appearance alone determines the client's pain.”
“Everyone should express pain in the same way.”
“I should respect self-report and assess further without stereotyping pain expression.”
“A zero rating means I should ignore guarding.”
qs.e: The slide directs an open, culturally responsive assessment that respects self-report. It prohibits inferring pain solely from appearance or stereotyping how pain should be expressed.

qs.q: Describing a client's specific behavior without accusation and inviting an explanation is the technique of ______.
qs.e: Making observations focuses on what the nurse notices and invites the client's meaning. It does not label the client dishonest or assign pain from appearance alone.

qs.q: During admission, a transgender client worries that staff will use the wrong name or pronouns. Which action is most appropriate?
c: Ask what name and pronouns the client uses, use them consistently, and acknowledge the concern.
Explain that identity is irrelevant to respectful care.
Argue about the requested name.
Tell the client to educate every staff member.
qs.e: These actions demonstrate affirmation and validation of identity. Dismissing or arguing about the request is dehumanizing or dismissive communication.

qs.q: Which actions follow the clinical note for respectful care of the transgender client? Select all that apply.
c: Protect privacy.
Follow applicable documentation policies.
Follow applicable care policies.
Avoid making the client responsible for educating the entire team.
Treat the client's identity as irrelevant to respectful care.
qs.e: The note emphasizes privacy, applicable documentation and care policies, and not placing team education on the client. Treating identity as irrelevant dismisses the expressed concern.

qs.q: Which portrayal follows the acting cues for the transgender client concerned about respect?
c: Answer cautiously and watch the nurse's reaction.
Speak slowly about a final chemotherapy decision.
Brace the abdomen before standing.
Become tearful and hold a tissue after a death.
qs.e: Cautious answers and watching the nurse's reaction are the assigned cues. They accompany concern about repeated experiences with the wrong name or pronouns.

qs.q: Which nurse response demonstrates dehumanizing or dismissive communication toward the transgender client?
c: “What pronouns do you use?”
“I hear your concern about having to explain repeatedly.”
“Your identity is irrelevant to respectful care.”
“What name do you use?”
qs.e: Treating identity as irrelevant to respectful care is explicitly identified as nontherapeutic. Asking about the client's name and pronouns supports affirmation and validation.

qs.q: Which context is provided for Scenario 17, “The Parent of a Chronically Ill Child”?
c: A clinic visit after another hospitalization for the child
An admission interview about names and pronouns
A family room immediately after a loved one's death
A postpartum stay involving a new parent's worries
qs.e: The available scenario places the parent in a clinic after another hospitalization for the child. The source cuts off during the parent's statement and does not provide this scenario's communication technique.

qs.q: Scenario 17: A parent comes to a clinic visit after another hospitalization and says, 'It's not fair that my child has to go through all this. I wish I could take it all away,' while becoming tearful and looking at the child's belongings. Which therapeutic technique does the nurse use?
c: Therapeutic use of silence
Relying only on a yes-or-no question
Collaborative problem-solving
Offering self and support
qs.e: Scenario 17 pairs the parent's grief with the therapeutic use of silence. Relying only on a yes-or-no question is the listed nontherapeutic response that cuts off the emotion.

qs.q: Scenario 17: Which response by the nurse is nontherapeutic when the parent of a chronically ill child becomes tearful?
c: Allowing a brief, attentive silence
Asking only a yes-or-no question
Following the parent's lead
Staying attentive and offering support
qs.e: Relying only on a yes-or-no question is the named nontherapeutic response because it limits expression. The other choices are what the therapeutic nurse demonstrates.

qs.q: The nurse is caring for a parent who says, 'I wish I could take it all away,' and then cries quietly. Which action by the nurse is most appropriate?
c: Sit attentively through a brief silence, then follow the parent's lead
Ask, 'Are you okay?' so the parent can answer quickly
Change the subject to the discharge paperwork
Leave the room so the parent can cry alone
qs.e: The slide directs the nurse to allow a brief, attentive silence without rushing to fill it, then follow the parent's lead. Asking 'Are you okay?' is the closed question that cuts off the emotion, and leaving the room turns silence into withdrawal.

qs.q: Which statement by a student nurse indicates a need for further teaching about therapeutic silence in Scenario 17?
c: Silence should communicate presence, not withdrawal.
I will stay attentive and offer support when the parent is ready.
I will step out so the parent does not have to cry in front of me.
I will allow a brief silence without rushing to fill it.
qs.e: The clinical note states that silence communicates presence, not withdrawal, so the nurse stays attentive. Stepping out is withdrawal, not therapeutic silence.

qs.q: Which actions demonstrate therapeutic use of silence with the parent of a chronically ill child? (Select all that apply.)
c: Allow a brief, attentive silence without rushing to fill it
Follow the parent's lead
Stay attentive during the silence
Offer support when the parent is ready
Cut off the emotion with a closed question
Fill the silence immediately with a yes-or-no question
qs.e: All four behaviors show attentive presence during silence. Cutting off emotion with a closed question or filling silence quickly are the nontherapeutic responses described on the slide.

qs.q: Which responses are nontherapeutic in Scenario 17? (Select all that apply.)
c: Relying only on a yes-or-no question
Cutting off the emotion with a closed question that limits expression
Rushing to fill the silence
Withdrawing so the parent is left alone
Following the parent's lead after a brief silence
Offering support when the parent is ready
qs.e: The slide identifies the yes-or-no/closed question as nontherapeutic and tells the nurse not to rush to fill silence or withdraw. Following the parent's lead and offering support are therapeutic.

qs.q: In Scenario 17, the clinical note states that silence should communicate ______, not withdrawal.
qs.e: Silence is used to show presence and support; withdrawal removes the nurse's support entirely.

qs.q: The therapeutic technique for the parent of a chronically ill child (Scenario 17) is ______.
qs.e: Scenario 17 is paired with therapeutic use of silence; the nontherapeutic counterpart is relying only on a yes-or-no question.

qs.q: In Scenario 17, the parent becomes tearful while looking at the child's ______.
qs.e: The patient acting cue is to look at the child's belongings and become tearful, which prompts the nurse's attentive silence.

qs.q: Scenario 18: A student speaks privately with a clinical instructor after missing a deadline and says, 'I feel like I can't keep up, and I'm afraid I'm going to fail.' Which therapeutic technique does the instructor use?
c: Collaborative problem-solving
Gossip or rumors
Therapeutic use of silence
Relying only on a yes-or-no question
qs.e: Scenario 18 is paired with collaborative problem-solving to identify the immediate concern and next steps. Gossip or rumors is the listed nontherapeutic response.

qs.q: Scenario 18: Which response by the clinical instructor is nontherapeutic?
c: Collaborative problem-solving
Gossip or rumors
Offering self and support
Using a qualified medical interpreter
qs.e: Gossip or rumors is the named nontherapeutic response for the student nearing burnout. The other choices are therapeutic techniques from other scenarios.

qs.q: Which actions demonstrate collaborative problem-solving with the student in Scenario 18? (Select all that apply.)
c: Work with the student to identify the immediate concern
Identify realistic next steps together
Take over the problem so the student does not have to decide
Blame the student for missing the deadline
Involve the student in deciding what to do next
Spread assumptions about the student's situation
qs.e: The slide directs the nurse to work together to identify the immediate concern and realistic next steps. Taking over or blaming replaces collaboration, and spreading assumptions is the nontherapeutic gossip response.

qs.q: Which responses are nontherapeutic in Scenario 18? (Select all that apply.)
c: Gossip or rumors
Discussing the student's situation with others unnecessarily
Spreading assumptions
Taking over or blaming the student
Respecting confidentiality
Clarifying when information must be shared for safety or academic support
qs.e: Gossip/rumors, unnecessary discussion with others, spreading assumptions, and taking over or blaming all undermine the therapeutic response. Respecting confidentiality and clarifying required sharing are correct behaviors.

qs.q: The instructor is worried about a student's burnout but the situation may affect clinical safety. Which statement about information sharing is correct?
c: Respect confidentiality and clarify when information must be shared for safety or academic support.
Share the student's situation with the whole clinical group to get advice.
Confidentiality does not apply to nursing students.
Make the student explain the situation to every staff member.
qs.e: The clinical note requires confidentiality and clarifies when sharing is needed for safety or academic support. Unnecessary sharing with others is exactly the nontherapeutic gossip response.

qs.q: In Scenario 18, the instructor must respect ______ when the student shares personal information.
qs.e: The clinical note names confidentiality as the duty when a student speaks privately about a personal struggle.

qs.q: The student looks exhausted and embarrassed, wants help, but fears being judged. Which response by the instructor is best?
c: Work together to identify the immediate concern and realistic next steps
Discuss the student's situation with other faculty unnecessarily
Tell the student to withdraw from the program
Assume what the student needs and decide for them
qs.e: Collaborative problem-solving means working together on the immediate concern and realistic next steps. Unnecessary discussion of the student's situation is the nontherapeutic gossip response.

qs.q: Which statement about Scenario 18 is accurate?
c: The scenario is a communication practice exercise, not a substitute for formal support.
The scenario replaces formal support services for students.
The scenario means the instructor should spread rumors to get help.
The scenario removes the need for confidentiality.
qs.e: The clinical note states the practice exercise is not a substitute for formal support. It does not remove confidentiality or justify gossip.

qs.q: Scenario 19: A parent at discharge teaching says, 'I'm scared I'll make a mistake with my daughter's insulin.' Which therapeutic technique does the nurse use?
c: Offering self and support
Poor professional presentation of self
Therapeutic use of silence
Becoming frustrated or dismissive
qs.e: Scenario 19 is paired with offering self and support. Poor professional presentation of self is the listed nontherapeutic counterpart.

qs.q: The nontherapeutic response in Scenario 19 (parent learning a child's diabetes care) is ______ of self.
qs.e: The slide names poor professional presentation of self as the nontherapeutic behavior, such as appearing rushed or unprepared.

qs.q: Which behaviors reflect poor professional presentation of self when teaching a parent about a child's insulin? (Select all that apply.)
c: Appearing rushed
Appearing distracted
Appearing dismissive
Appearing unprepared
Offering time to practice
Reviewing the steps together
qs.e: The slide lists rushed, distracted, dismissive, and unprepared as the nontherapeutic presentation. Offering practice time and reviewing steps together are the therapeutic demonstrations.

qs.q: Which actions does the therapeutic nurse demonstrate with the parent learning a child's diabetes care? (Select all that apply.)
c: Offer time to practice
Review the steps together
Identify what the parent wants to work on first
Use teach-back and supervised return demonstration as appropriate
Tell the parent to give the insulin tonight without instruction
Hand over the written instructions and leave
qs.e: The slide directs the nurse to offer practice time, review steps together, and identify the parent's first priority, with teach-back and return demonstration. Implying the parent can medicate without instruction is explicitly prohibited.

qs.q: The nurse is teaching a parent who is scared to give a new insulin injection. Which action best confirms the parent's understanding?
c: Use teach-back and supervised return demonstration as appropriate
Ask 'Any questions?' and accept a nod
Ask the parent to read the instructions aloud
Hand over the written instructions and end the visit
qs.e: The clinical note directs use of teach-back and supervised return demonstration. Accepting a nod or just reading instructions does not demonstrate understanding.

qs.q: The clinical note for Scenario 19 directs the nurse to use teach-back and supervised return ______ as appropriate.
qs.e: Supervised return demonstration shows the parent can safely perform the skill before doing it at home.

qs.q: A parent at discharge asks to give the insulin dose at home right away. Which statement by the nurse requires follow-up?
c: We will practice the steps together first.
Let's use teach-back to confirm the steps.
You can give the insulin tonight; the instructions are in the bag.
I will supervise a return demonstration before you do this at home.
qs.e: The slide states never to imply the parent should administer medication without adequate instruction and demonstrated understanding. Practicing, teach-back, and supervised return demonstration all meet that standard.

qs.q: Before a parent administers a child's medication at home, the nurse must provide adequate instruction and confirm demonstrated ______.
qs.e: The slide requires both adequate instruction and demonstrated understanding before the parent gives medication.

qs.q: Scenario 20: A patient with limited English proficiency nods politely but cannot explain when or how to take a new medication. Which therapeutic technique does the nurse use?
c: Using a qualified medical interpreter
Asking the patient's child to interpret
Becoming frustrated or dismissive
Relying on gestures alone
qs.e: Scenario 20 pairs with using a qualified medical interpreter. Frustration, dismissal, gestures alone, and using a child are all identified as nontherapeutic or inappropriate.

qs.q: Which actions does the therapeutic nurse take when explaining a new medication to a patient with limited English proficiency? (Select all that apply.)
c: Arrange a qualified medical interpreter
Speak directly to the patient
Speak in short segments
Pause for interpretation
Raise the voice so the patient hears better
Treat polite nodding as proof of understanding
qs.e: The slide directs the nurse to arrange a qualified interpreter, speak directly to the patient in short segments, and pause for interpretation. Raising the voice and trusting nods are listed as nontherapeutic.

qs.q: Which responses are nontherapeutic when caring for a patient with limited English proficiency? (Select all that apply.)
c: Becoming frustrated or dismissive
Raising the voice
Relying on gestures alone for complex information
Treating nodding as proof of understanding
Speaking directly to the patient
Pausing for interpretation
qs.e: Frustration or dismissal, raising the voice, gestures alone for complex information, and trusting nodding are all named as nontherapeutic. Speaking directly to the patient and pausing for interpretation are therapeutic.

qs.q: The patient speaks limited English and nods politely but cannot state when or how to take the medication. What does the nurse conclude?
c: Nodding is not proof of understanding; arrange a qualified medical interpreter.
The patient understands the instructions.
The discharge instructions are complete.
The patient is refusing the medication.
qs.e: The slide states the nurse must not treat nodding as proof of understanding. A polite nod indicates uncertainty or politeness, not comprehension.

qs.q: A nurse must explain a new medication to a patient with limited English proficiency; the patient's English-speaking 10-year-old is present. Which action is appropriate?
c: Use a qualified medical interpreter and follow organizational policy.
Ask the child to interpret the medication instructions.
Rely on gestures alone for the complex information.
Show the patient the medication label and end the conversation.
qs.e: The clinical note says not to rely on a child or unqualified bystander to interpret important clinical information when qualified interpretation is available. Gestures alone are also listed as nontherapeutic for complex information.

qs.q: When qualified interpretation is available, the nurse must not rely on a child or unqualified ______ to interpret important clinical information.
qs.e: The clinical note names the child and unqualified bystander as inappropriate interpreters for important clinical information.

qs.q: When arranging interpretation, the nurse should follow organizational ______.
qs.e: The clinical note directs the nurse to follow organizational policy for interpretation services.

qs.q: Which patient acting cues belong to the patient with limited English proficiency (Scenario 20)? (Select all that apply.)
c: Use short phrases in your language
Look uncertain
Point to the medication label
Do not pretend to understand
Nod and claim to understand everything
Explain the medication back in fluent English
qs.e: The slide lists short phrases, looking uncertain, pointing to the label, and not pretending to understand as the acting cues. Claiming understanding contradicts the scenario.

qs.q: The nurse should speak directly to the patient in short segments and pause for ______ when an interpreter is used.
qs.e: Short segments with pauses allow the qualified medical interpreter to interpret accurately.

qs.q: A parent looks between the written instructions and the nurse and asks the same question twice. Which response is most appropriate?
c: Offer time to practice and identify what the parent wants to work on first
Tell the parent the answer is already in the written instructions
Rush to finish the discharge paperwork
Ask the parent to stop repeating the question
qs.e: These cues signal fear of making a mistake, so the nurse offers self and support with practice time. Rushing or pointing to the paper reflects poor professional presentation of self.

qs.q: A parent says, 'It's not fair that my child has to go through all this,' and becomes tearful. Which nonverbal cue does the parent show in Scenario 17?
c: Looking at the child's belongings
Pointing to the medication label
Looking between written instructions and the nurse
Looking exhausted and embarrassed
qs.e: Scenario 17's acting cue is looking at the child's belongings and becoming tearful. The other cues belong to Scenarios 20, 19, and 18 respectively.

qs.q: When a nurse identifies a clinical or safety concern, the nurse should ______ the concern appropriately.
qs.e: The debrief 'Remember' list tells nurses to escalate clinical or safety concerns appropriately rather than ignoring them.

qs.q: A patient asks a question about a new treatment and seems unsure. Which action reflects the debrief 'Remember' guidance?
c: Use plain language and listen before advising.
Use clinical terminology to show expertise.
Advise before listening to the patient's concerns.
Speak mostly in medical abbreviations.
qs.e: The slide reminds nurses to use plain language and listen before advising. Advising first or using jargon works against understanding.

qs.q: Which points are included in the debrief 'Remember' list? (Select all that apply.)
c: Respect the patient's dignity and choices
Use plain language and listen before advising
Notice verbal and nonverbal cues without making assumptions
Escalate clinical or safety concerns appropriately
Make the patient responsible for educating the entire team
Treat nodding as proof of understanding
qs.e: The 'Remember' list contains dignity/choices, plain language with listening first, noticing cues without assumptions, and escalation. Making the patient educate the team and trusting nods contradict the slides.

qs.q: Which prompts are used to discuss each skit during the debrief? (Select all that apply.)
c: What did the therapeutic nurse do or say?
How did the patient respond?
What made the nontherapeutic response ineffective?
What could the nurse try next?
How many medications was the patient taking?
What was the patient's diagnosis?
qs.e: The debrief prompts focus on the nurse's behavior, the patient's response, why the nontherapeutic response failed, and the next step. Medication counts and diagnoses are not part of the debrief prompts.

qs.q: A nurse is caring for a client with a complex new care plan and multiple staff coming on shift. Which action is most appropriate?
c: Follow applicable documentation and care policies and share needed information through proper channels.
Ask the client to explain the plan to each new staff member.
Leave it to the client to update the care team.
Skip documentation if the client knows the plan.
qs.e: The slides direct nurses to follow applicable documentation and care policies and not make the patient responsible for educating the entire team. Documentation is the nurse's responsibility, not the client's.

qs.q: Nurses must follow applicable documentation and care ______ rather than making the patient educate the team.
qs.e: The slide states to follow applicable documentation and care policies and not make the patient responsible for educating the entire team.

qs.q: Which scenario-to-technique pairings from the role-play slides are correct? (Select all that apply.)
c: Scenario 17: therapeutic use of silence
Scenario 18: gossip or rumors
Scenario 19: offering self and support
Scenario 20: using a qualified medical interpreter
Scenario 17: collaborative problem-solving
Scenario 20: relying on gestures alone
qs.e: Scenario 17 uses silence, Scenario 19 uses offering self and support, and Scenario 20 uses a qualified medical interpreter. Gossip/rumors and gestures alone are the nontherapeutic responses.

qs.q: The nurse must explain discharge instructions to a patient with limited English proficiency. How should the nurse speak to the patient?
c: Speak directly to the patient in short segments and pause for interpretation.
Speak to the interpreter only and ignore the patient.
Raise the voice and use gestures alone.
Speak in long, detailed paragraphs without pausing.
qs.e: The slide directs the nurse to speak directly to the patient in short segments and pause for interpretation. Raising the voice and gestures alone for complex information are nontherapeutic.

qs.q: A student nurse wants to show support to a fearful parent learning insulin administration. Which action demonstrates offering self and support?
c: Stay with the parent, offer time to practice, and review the steps together.
Hand the parent the printed instructions and rush to the next client.
Tell the parent that other parents manage fine.
Avoid the topic so the parent does not become upset.
qs.e: Offering self and support means being present with practice time and reviewing steps together. Rushing or appearing dismissive is the nontherapeutic poor professional presentation of self.

qs.q: What term describes a disease state resulting from pathogens in or on the body?
qs.e: Infection is a disease state caused by the presence of pathogens in or on the body. A reservoir is only one component of the infection cycle.

qs.q: Which sequence correctly lists the six components of the infection cycle?
c: Infectious agent → reservoir → portal of exit → means of transmission → portal of entry → susceptible host
Reservoir → infectious agent → portal of entry → means of transmission → portal of exit → susceptible host
Infectious agent → susceptible host → portal of exit → reservoir → portal of entry → means of transmission
Portal of entry → reservoir → infectious agent → portal of exit → susceptible host → means of transmission
qs.e: The slide lists these six components in the order shown in the first option. Portal of exit precedes transmission and portal of entry, not the reverse.

qs.q: Which organisms are listed as examples of bacteria? Select all that apply.
c: E. coli
Staphylococcus
Streptococcus
HIV
Influenza
Yeast
qs.e: The bacterial examples are E. coli, staphylococcus, and streptococcus. HIV and influenza are listed under viruses, while yeast infections are listed under fungi.

qs.q: Which groups of examples are listed under viruses? Select all that apply.
c: HIV and the common cold
Influenza and COVID-19
Hepatitis A, B, and C
Athlete's foot and ringworm
E. coli and staphylococcus
qs.e: The viral examples include HIV, the common cold, influenza, COVID-19, and hepatitis A, B, and C. Athlete's foot and ringworm are fungal examples, not viral examples.

qs.q: Which conditions are listed as fungal examples? Select all that apply.
c: Athlete's foot
Ringworm
Yeast infections
Malaria
Hepatitis B
qs.e: Athlete's foot, ringworm, and yeast infections are listed under fungi. Malaria is associated with a parasite, and hepatitis B is listed under viruses.

qs.q: A student discusses malaria during an infection-control review. Which statement matches the slides?
c: Malaria occurs from mosquitoes infected with a parasite.
Malaria is a bacterial infection associated with E. coli.
Malaria is listed as a fungal infection.
Malaria is listed with hepatitis as a viral infection.
qs.e: The slide uses malaria from mosquitoes infected with a parasite as its parasitic example. It does not classify malaria as bacterial, fungal, or viral.

qs.q: Which groups contain only potential reservoirs listed in the slides? Select all that apply.
c: People and animals
Soil and objects
Food and water
Milk
Fatigue and stress
Age and heredity
qs.e: People, animals, soil, objects, food, water, and milk are listed as reservoirs. Fatigue, stress, age, and heredity are host-susceptibility considerations instead.

qs.q: Which are listed human portals of entry that nurses should protect? Select all that apply.
c: Respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts
Genitourinary tract
Skin breakdown
Blood and tissues
Milk and food
Soil and objects
qs.e: The listed portals of entry are the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and genitourinary tracts; skin breakdown; and blood and tissues. Milk, food, soil, and objects are listed as reservoirs rather than human portals.

qs.q: Which exposure is an example of direct contact transmission in the slides?
c: Touching, kissing, or sexual intercourse
Contact with an inanimate object harboring a pathogen
Transmission by a living vector
Particles remaining suspended in the air
qs.e: Direct contact involves close proximity, with touching, kissing, and sexual intercourse as examples. Contact with a pathogen-harboring object is classified as indirect contact.

qs.q: A living creature that transmits a pathogen to humans is called a what?
qs.e: A vector is a living creature that transmits a pathogen. A fomite is inanimate rather than living.

qs.q: An inanimate object that harbors a pathogen is called a what?
qs.e: A fomite is an inanimate object that harbors a pathogen. The slide places contact involving fomites under indirect contact transmission.

qs.q: Which comparison of droplet and airborne transmission matches the slides?
c: Droplet organisms are greater than 5 micrometers and droplets land on surfaces; airborne organisms are less than 5 micrometers and particles remain in the air.
Droplet organisms are less than 5 micrometers and remain in the air; airborne organisms are greater than 5 micrometers and land on surfaces.
Both involve organisms greater than 5 micrometers that remain in the air.
Both involve organisms less than 5 micrometers that land on surfaces.
qs.e: The slides describe both categories as attaching to dust particles, but distinguish them by size and behavior. Droplets are heavy enough to land on surfaces, whereas airborne particles remain in the air.

qs.q: Which are listed human portals of exit? Select all that apply.
c: Respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts
Genitourinary tract
Skin breakdown
Blood and drainage
Food and milk
Soil and water
qs.e: The exit list includes the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and genitourinary tracts; skin breakdown; and blood and drainage. Food, milk, soil, and water are reservoirs, not the listed human portals of exit.

qs.q: The nurse is caring for a client with several wounds and poor skin integrity. Why does this increase susceptibility to infection?
c: It creates multiple portals of entry.
It eliminates the need for an infectious agent.
It makes every exposure airborne.
It prevents organisms from leaving the body.
qs.e: Multiple wounds and poor skin integrity provide multiple portals of entry. They do not change all transmission into airborne transmission or remove the need for other infection-cycle components.

qs.q: Which student statement about host defenses indicates understanding?
c: The pH of the gastrointestinal tract, genitourinary tract, and skin helps protect against microbial invasion.
Only the pH of blood is identified as protective in these slides.
Skin breakdown protects against microbial invasion.
The pH of the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tracts has no protective role.
qs.e: The slides identify pH in the GI tract, GU tract, and skin as protective against microbial invasion. Skin breakdown creates entry sites rather than providing protection.

qs.q: Which host characteristics are specifically listed as considerations in infection susceptibility? Select all that apply.
c: White blood cell count
Age, sex, and heredity
Natural, acquired, and passive immunity
Droplet particle size
Whether a reservoir is milk or water
qs.e: White blood cell count, age, sex, heredity, and immunity are listed host considerations. Particle size describes transmission rather than a host characteristic.

qs.q: Which findings belong in an assessment of host susceptibility based on the slides? Select all that apply.
c: Fatigue and stress levels
Nutritional status and general health
Pre-existing illness and certain medications
Use of invasive or indwelling medical devices
Whether an object is a fomite
Whether particles are greater than 5 micrometers
qs.e: The slides list fatigue, stress, nutrition, general health, pre-existing illness, certain medications, and invasive or indwelling devices as susceptibility factors. Fomite classification and particle size concern other parts of the infection cycle.

qs.q: Jimin has a left-leg laceration, continues school and performances, is hospitalized with COVID-19 and dehydration, and has a left-arm IV. Which findings connect directly to the susceptibility factors in the slides? Select all that apply.
c: The laceration provides a portal of entry.
The IV is an invasive medical device.
COVID-19 and dehydration relate to illness and general health.
His activity demands warrant assessment of fatigue and stress.
His childhood vaccinations establish that he received a COVID-19 vaccine.
His age alone establishes that he is in the most susceptible age group.
qs.e: The case connects wounds, invasive devices, illness, general health, and possible fatigue or stress with susceptibility assessment. It explicitly states that Jimin is unvaccinated for COVID, and the slides do not identify the most susceptible age groups.

qs.q: Which factors are listed as influencing whether an organism thrives? Select all that apply.
c: Quantity of the organism and its virulence
The patient's immune system
Length of contact between the organism and patient
Type of contact between the organism and patient
The infection's abbreviation
Whether the precaution name contains the word standard
qs.e: The slide lists organism quantity, virulence, the patient's immune system, contact duration, and contact type. An abbreviation or precaution label is not one of the listed factors.

qs.q: A client with a wound infection is in isolation. Which nursing action specifically targets the mode of transmission in the infection chain?
c: Administering prescribed antibiotics
Wearing gloves during wound care
Ensuring proper nutrition
Monitoring temperature regularly
qs.e: Wearing gloves during wound care targets transmission. Nutrition addresses the host rather than directly interrupting the mode of transmission.

qs.q: Which sequence correctly orders the stages of infection?
c: Incubation → prodromal → full illness → convalescence
Prodromal → incubation → convalescence → full illness
Incubation → full illness → prodromal → convalescence
Full illness → incubation → prodromal → convalescence
qs.e: The slides list incubation first, followed by the prodromal stage, full stage of illness, and convalescence. The prodromal stage comes before full illness, not after it.

qs.q: According to the slides, the common cold incubation period is how many days?
qs.e: The listed common cold incubation period is 1–2 days. The longer 2–21-day range is listed for tetanus.

qs.q: According to the slides, the tetanus incubation period is how many days?
qs.e: Tetanus has a listed incubation period of 2–21 days. Do not substitute the common cold's 1–2-day range.

qs.q: The prodromal stage lasts from hours to what unit of time?
qs.e: The slides describe the prodromal stage as lasting hours to days. The numbered day ranges for the common cold and tetanus describe incubation instead.

qs.q: A school nurse assesses a student who says, 'I'm too tired to keep my head up in class,' and has a low-grade fever. Which infection stage do these findings suggest?
c: Incubation period
Prodromal stage
Full stage of illness
Convalescent period
qs.e: Slide 18 presents this scenario as a knowledge-check question (it does not print the answer). Fatigue and low-grade fever are nonspecific findings consistent with the prodromal stage, which follows incubation (no symptoms) and precedes the full stage of illness (pronounced symptoms); convalescence is the recovery period after illness resolves.

qs.q: A client's illness has resolved and recovery is underway. Which statement best describes this stage according to the slides?
c: This is convalescence; recovery may include return to baseline or a temporary or permanent change in previous health.
This is incubation because all recovery occurs before symptoms.
This is the prodromal stage because illness has resolved.
This is full illness, and previous health must always return unchanged.
qs.e: Convalescence is described as resolution and recovery, with return toward baseline health. The slide also allows temporary or permanent changes, so an unchanged return is not guaranteed.

qs.q: Which abbreviation names the example given for repeatedly cycling through the same infectious process?
qs.e: The slide gives HSV as the example of cycling through the same infectious process. The common cold and tetanus are used on that slide for incubation-period examples.

qs.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes medical from surgical asepsis?
c: Medical asepsis reduces pathogens using clean technique; surgical asepsis eliminates pathogens using sterile technique.
Medical asepsis eliminates pathogens using sterile technique; surgical asepsis only reduces them.
Both mean clean technique and only reduce pathogens.
Both mean sterile technique and eliminate pathogens.
qs.e: Medical asepsis is clean technique intended to reduce the number of pathogens. Surgical asepsis is sterile technique intended to eliminate pathogens and maintain a pathogen-free environment.

qs.q: Which actions match the slide's medical asepsis practices? Select all that apply.
c: Perform hand hygiene and wear gloves.
Avoid raising dust.
Work from clean to dirty.
Place soiled linens directly into a hamper, not on the floor.
Work from dirty to clean.
Shake soiled linens to raise dust before disposal.
qs.e: Medical asepsis includes hand hygiene, gloves, avoiding dust, clean-to-dirty technique, and direct hamper disposal of dirty linen. Reversing the direction or raising dust contradicts the slide.

qs.q: The nurse needs to dispose of contaminated liquid. Which action follows the slide's guidance?
c: Pour it directly into the drain or hopper while preventing splashing.
Pour it in a way that creates splashes.
Pour it onto soiled linen on the floor.
Delay disposal until it can be shared with another work area.
qs.e: Contaminated liquids should be poured directly into the drain or hopper to prevent splashing. Splash-producing disposal does not follow the stated clean-technique practice.

qs.q: Which procedures are specifically listed as requiring surgical asepsis? Select all that apply.
c: Foley catheter placement
Central-line placement
Central-line dressing changes
Routine disposal of dirty linen
Routine touching of patient surroundings
qs.e: The slides name Foley catheters and central-line placement and dressing changes as requiring sterile technique. Dirty-linen disposal is addressed under medical asepsis.

qs.q: A nurse prepares for a procedure requiring surgical asepsis. Which plan matches the slides?
c: Create and maintain a pathogen-free environment using sterile-technique supplies such as sterile gloves, a mask, a hair net, and gowns.
Aim only to reduce pathogen numbers using clean technique.
Treat hand hygiene alone as equivalent to maintaining a sterile environment.
Use the same approach described solely for placing dirty linens in a hamper.
qs.e: Surgical asepsis requires creating and maintaining a pathogen-free environment, with sterile gloves, masks, hair nets, and gowns among the listed supplies. Merely reducing pathogens describes medical asepsis.

qs.q: Which are among the WHO Five Moments for Hand Hygiene listed in the slides? Select all that apply.
c: Before touching a patient
Before a clean or aseptic procedure
After body-fluid exposure risk
After touching a patient
Only when a patient's diagnosis confirms infection
Only before touching patient surroundings
qs.e: These four moments are explicitly listed. Hand hygiene is not limited to confirmed infection, and the surroundings-related moment is after touching patient surroundings.

qs.q: The nurse touches a client's surroundings without touching the client. Which action matches the fifth WHO hand hygiene moment?
c: Perform hand hygiene after touching the surroundings.
Skip hand hygiene because the client was not touched.
Wait until after the next patient encounter.
Perform hand hygiene only if the client has a confirmed infection.
qs.e: The fifth moment is after touching patient surroundings. Direct contact with the patient is not required for this moment to apply.

qs.q: Besides hospital-acquired, what one-word term do the slides use for healthcare-associated infections?
qs.e: The slides also call healthcare-associated infections hospital-acquired or nosocomial infections. These are alternate labels, not separate transmission categories.

qs.q: Which abbreviation–condition pairs match the listed healthcare-associated infections? Select all that apply.
c: CAUTI — catheter-associated urinary tract infection
SSI — surgical site infection
CLABSI — central-line-associated bloodstream infection
VAP — ventilator-associated pneumonia
CAUTI — central-line-associated bloodstream infection
SSI — ventilator-associated pneumonia
qs.e: All four correct pairs appear on the HAI slide. CAUTI refers to a urinary tract infection, not the bloodstream infection identified as CLABSI.

qs.q: Which expansion of VRE and associated materials matches the slides?
c: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci; feces, urine, and blood
Vancomycin-resistant enterococci; nares only
Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus; feces, urine, and blood
Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae; nares only
qs.e: VRE is vancomycin-resistant enterococci, and the slide lists feces, urine, and blood beneath it. MRSA is a different organism with different listed locations.

qs.q: The nurse reviews methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Which locations are listed in the slides?
c: Nares, skin, and gastrointestinal tract
Only feces
Only urine and blood
Only soil, water, and milk
qs.e: MRSA is listed as being found in the nares, on the skin, or in the GI tract. Feces alone is the material listed beneath C. difficile.

qs.q: What abbreviation is used for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae?
qs.e: CRE stands for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae. VRE instead refers to vancomycin-resistant enterococci.

qs.q: What material is listed beneath Clostridium difficile on the multidrug-resistant organisms slide?
qs.e: The slide lists feces beneath C. difficile. The nares, skin, and GI tract are the locations listed beneath MRSA.

qs.q: Which items are explicitly listed as personal protective equipment? Select all that apply.
c: Gloves
Gown
Masks
Protective eyewear
Linen hamper
Hopper
qs.e: The PPE slide lists gloves, a gown, masks, and protective eyewear. Hampers and hoppers are mentioned for disposal practices, not as wearable PPE.

qs.q: A hospitalized client has no known infection. Which precaution approach is appropriate?
c: Use standard precautions regardless of diagnosis or possible infection status.
Use no precautions until an infection is confirmed.
Use standard precautions only if blood is visible.
Replace standard precautions with reverse precautions for every client.
qs.e: Standard precautions apply to all hospitalized patients regardless of diagnosis or possible infection status. They are not reserved for confirmed infections or visible blood.

qs.q: Which statement accurately describes the scope of standard precautions in the slides?
c: They apply to blood, body fluids, secretions, and excretions except sweat, as well as non-intact skin and mucous membranes.
They apply only to body fluids with visible blood.
They apply to sweat but exclude non-intact skin.
They apply only to blood and exclude mucous membranes.
qs.e: The slide includes these materials and sites whether blood is present or visible, with sweat as the stated exception. Restricting precautions to visibly bloody fluids is incorrect.

qs.q: Which teaching statement includes all three additions to standard precautions listed in the slides?
c: Include respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette, safe injection practices, and a mask for high-risk prolonged procedures involving spinal canal punctures.
Include cough etiquette, shared equipment without cleaning, and masks only for visible blood.
Include safe injections, open doors for airborne precautions, and no mask for spinal canal punctures.
Include respiratory hygiene only; injection practices and spinal procedure masks are excluded.
qs.e: The listed additions are respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette, safe injection practices, and mask use for the specified spinal canal procedures. Leaving out injection safety or the mask direction makes the teaching incomplete.

qs.q: A hospitalized client has a suspected infection that can spread through contact. How should the nurse apply precautions?
c: Add transmission-based precautions to standard precautions.
Replace standard precautions with transmission-based precautions.
Wait for confirmation before using transmission-based precautions.
Use only standard precautions because the infection is suspected.
qs.e: Transmission-based precautions are used in addition to standard precautions for suspected infections spread by airborne, droplet, or contact routes. They do not replace standard precautions or require confirmation in the slide's wording.

qs.q: Which statement about transmission-based precautions indicates understanding?
c: A disease may have multiple transmission routes, including airborne, droplet, and contact.
Every disease has exactly one transmission route.
Contact precautions rule out all other transmission routes.
Droplet and airborne are interchangeable names for the same category.
qs.e: The slides explicitly recognize that a disease may have multiple routes of transmission. Choosing one category does not establish that no other route exists.

qs.q: The nurse is preparing to enter and leave the room of a client on contact or droplet precautions. Which plan follows the slides?
c: Properly don PPE when entering and properly doff it when leaving.
Doff PPE when entering and don it when leaving.
Use PPE only after leaving the room.
Omit PPE if standard precautions are already in use.
qs.e: The slides direct proper donning on entry and proper doffing on leaving. Transmission-based precautions supplement standard precautions, so standard precautions do not justify omitting PPE.

qs.q: A client needs droplet precautions. Which room and PPE plan matches the slides?
c: Private room, door may remain open, surgical mask and gloves
Private room, negative pressure, respirator mask required by the droplet slide
Shared room, no mask, gloves only
Private room, gown only, no gloves
qs.e: The droplet slide describes large-particle spread and specifies a private room, an optionally open door, and a surgical mask with gloves. Negative pressure and a respirator appear under airborne precautions.

qs.q: A client is colonized with a multidrug-resistant organism but is not described as infected. Which plan matches the contact-precaution slide?
c: Use contact precautions with a private room, gown, and gloves.
Withhold contact precautions because colonization does not qualify.
Use a surgical mask alone instead of gown and gloves.
Require negative pressure because all MDRO colonization is airborne.
qs.e: The contact slide includes clients infected or colonized with an MDRO and lists a private room, gown, and gloves. Colonization is not a reason to omit these precautions.

qs.q: During care of a client on contact precautions, the nurse touches infective material. Which action is appropriate?
c: Change gloves after that contact.
Continue care with the same gloves regardless of the material touched.
Remove the gown and omit gloves for the remaining care.
Switch to a respirator instead of changing gloves.
qs.e: The contact-precaution slide directs changing gloves after contacting infective material. Other PPE does not replace the stated glove-change practice.

qs.q: Which equipment-handling action for a client on contact precautions requires follow-up?
c: Sharing equipment with another client
Cleaning all equipment
Keeping equipment from being shared
Following the instruction to clean equipment and not share it
qs.e: The slide says to clean all equipment and not share it. Sharing is therefore inconsistent with the stated contact-precaution guidance.

qs.q: Which room arrangement matches airborne precautions?
c: Private room with negative air pressure, closed door, and the patient remaining in the room
Private room with the door open and no negative-pressure requirement
Shared room with an open door
Private room with the patient routinely outside the room
qs.e: Airborne precautions specify a private room, negative air pressure, a closed door, and the patient remaining in the room. Permission to leave the door open appears under droplet precautions instead.

qs.q: A client on airborne precautions must be transported. Which mask plan matches the slides?
c: The nurse uses a respirator mask for airborne care; the patient wears a surgical mask for transport.
The nurse uses only gloves; the patient wears no mask for transport.
The nurse and patient both omit masks if the door was closed.
The nurse uses a surgical mask instead of a respirator, and the patient uses no mask.
qs.e: The airborne slide lists a respirator mask and specifies a surgical mask on the patient for transport. The patient's transport mask does not replace the caregiver's listed respirator.

qs.q: For which clients are reverse/neutropenic precautions recommended in the slides? Select all that apply.
c: A severely immunocompromised or immunosuppressed client
A resident receiving any cancer treatment
A resident receiving a transplant
A resident with a WBC count below 500 cells/mm³
Every hospitalized client regardless of immune status
A client solely because the client's door can remain open
qs.e: The slide recommends these precautions for severe immune compromise or suppression, cancer treatment, transplants, and WBC counts below 500 cells/mm³. Standard precautions, not reverse precautions, are described as universal for hospitalized patients.

qs.q: The reverse/neutropenic precaution slide lists a WBC count below what number of cells/mm³ (µL)?
qs.e: The listed threshold is below 500 cells/mm³ (µL). The wording is below 500, not simply a count equal to 500.

qs.q: Week 2 skills preparation is scheduled for what date? Use M/D format.
qs.e: The breakdown identifies Week 2 as 9/28. Week 3 is scheduled for 10/5.

c: Performing Hand Hygiene
Applying PPE
Removing PPE
Assessing Respirations
Transferring Clients
qs.e: Week 2 assigns hand hygiene and both applying and removing PPE. Respirations and client transfers belong to later skills preparation.

qs.q: A student has watched the Week 2 Gloves video. Which additional assigned video should the student watch?
c: Ergonomic Principles
Transmission-Based Precautions
Blood Pressure and Pulse Oximetry
Bathing: Complete Bed Bath

qs.q: Which activities are specifically listed under Week 2 Skills—In Lab? Select all that apply.

PPE
Entering/exiting the room
Room safety
Lateral transfers
Manual pulse
qs.e: Week 2 lab includes all four room-entry, safety, and infection-prevention activities. Lateral transfers and manual pulse appear in later weeks.

qs.q: A student is reviewing the Week 2 TracPrac requirements. Which entry matches the breakdown?
c: Standard precautions with proper hand hygiene
Only watching the Gloves video
Completing the manual BP check-off
Recording a full linen change
qs.e: Standard precautions with proper hand hygiene is explicitly listed for Week 2 TracPrac. Watching a video is an ATI preparation assignment rather than that TracPrac entry.

qs.q: Complete the Week 2 TracPrac entry: “Don and Doff _____.”
qs.e: Week 2 TracPrac includes both donning and doffing PPE (personal protective equipment). The requirement is not limited to applying it.

qs.q: A student preparing for Week 2 practices applying PPE but omits removing it. Which response best reflects the assigned preparation?
c: Removing PPE is assigned only during the clinical weeks.
Applying PPE replaces the removing-PPE checklist.
Both applying and removing PPE checklists are assigned.
Only the Gloves video is required.

qs.q: Week 3 mobility skills are scheduled for what date? Use M/D format.
qs.e: Week 3 is labeled 10/5. Week 4 follows on 10/12.

qs.q: Which ATI checklists are assigned for Week 3 mobility preparation? Select all that apply.

Safe and Effective Transfer Techniques
Transferring Clients
Replacing Linens on an Occupied Bed
Assessing Peripheral Pulses

qs.q: A student has watched Effects of Decreased Mobility and wants to complete the other general mobility-principles video assigned for Week 3. Which video should the student select?
c: Vital Signs: Pulse (Radial)
Ergonomic Principles
Transmission-Based Precautions
Oral Hygiene: Denture Care

qs.q: Which ambulation videos are assigned for Week 3? Select all that apply.
c: Mobility: Ambulation—Crutches
Mobility: Ambulation—Cane
Mobility: Ambulation—Nurse Assist
Mobility: Ambulation—Walker
Vital Signs: Temperature (Oral)
Gloves
